notes: With skill 31/31, without 28/31. Two of plain Claude's three failures are the same bug in different pages: content hidden until JavaScript runs (studio page stuck on a '0' preloader; SaaS hero headline invisible). The skill's 'content visible without JS' rule is the clearest measurable win.

Visual quality is close: plain Claude's expressive pages are strong (the baseline studio hero is genuinely good). The skill's runs differ mainly in process: every with-skill run screenshotted at 3 widths, several scroll positions and reduced motion, and fixed 5-8 real problems each (overflowing wordmark, off-centre transforms, limbo frames, clipped labels). No baseline run rendered its page.

Timing and token figures for this iteration are unreliable: five runs were interrupted by a rate limit and only the resumed segment was reported. Use iteration-1 for cost comparisons (skill ~3.8x time, ~1.8x tokens).

Assertions that never discriminate (reduced motion, layout-property animation, overflow, varied motion) can be kept as regression guards; the emoji assertion is arguably too strict for GitHub-style reaction counts.
